what_worked: clip_qa cropping the frame around a victory-overlay window and directly OCR-reading the Chinese boss name text ('已击败 妖王·XXX') is a reliable way to disambiguate boss identity when the DB captioner failed to capture the name in text.

Deductive elimination (searching exhaustively for a name, finding zero hits, then reasoning from the surrounding named-boss timestamps) can substitute for visual confirmation and still reach the correct answer, as rollout-03 showed.

Cross-checking a nearby unnamed 'victory' episode against a clip_qa call before assuming it corresponds to the target boss (as rollout-01 did for the 16830-16900s window) prevents misattributing an unrelated boss kill.
transferable_lessons: When an entity/boss name never appears in any DB text table, do not assume the first nearby 'victory'/'defeated' episode belongs to it - verify with clip_qa by reading the on-screen name overlay, since multiple similarly-described boss fights can occur close together.

For temporal-ordering questions across bosses/events, cross-reference every candidate timestamp against the entities table's first_seen_s/last_seen_s (when available) before finalizing an order; this catches misattributions like confusing a snowy-arena boss (亢金龙) 6000s later for the target dragon.

When results diverge from a suspected-wrong reference answer, retrieval quality should be judged on evidence traceability (was the boss name actually read off-screen, or merely assumed?) rather than only on the final score - two of the best-evidenced rollouts here scored lowest.
